name: Availability Cascade
description: A self-reinforcing process in which an expressed perception gains plausibility simply because it is increasingly present in public discourse, driven by learning from others' apparent beliefs and by wanting social acceptance.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to how a vivid risk or story comes to dominate attention in feeds and reviews; design that amplifies what is already prominent can feed a cascade.
myth_risk_note: A plausible mechanism often cited as if it were an established empirical regularity; the corpus holds only the theory.
prevalence_note: Cited in risk regulation and media studies; rarely tested directly.

findings.description: Defines an availability cascade as a self-reinforcing process of collective belief formation in which an expressed perception gains plausibility through rising availability in public discourse, driven by informational and reputational motives; argues that 'availability entrepreneurs' can trigger cascades and proposes safeguards for risk regulation. A theoretical argument; the paper does not report an empirical test.
